key_insight: SearchOS-V1 proposes a robust multi-agent information-seeking system that helps web-search agents stay on track, avoid repetitive dead-ends, and recover when evidence is hard to find. In simple terms: it improves collaboration so search agents spend budget more efficiently and produce more complete answers.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a common failure mode in tool-integrated LLM search agents: as interaction histories grow, agents lose task progress, get stuck in repetitive search loops, and waste search budget without finding useful evidence.
method: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent collaboration framework for open-domain web search and information seeking.
Adds mechanisms to track task progress across long interaction histories so agents can better decide what has been tried and what remains unresolved.
Improves robustness when search attempts fail, helping agents avoid looping behaviors and coordinate more effectively toward the final answer.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means more reliable retrieval-augmented and web-search workflows with fewer wasted queries and better answer completeness. It is especially relevant for building practical agents that must operate under limited budgets and noisy, open-domain information.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing multiple agents collaborating across search, evidence tracking, and answer synthesis.
Loop-avoidance illustration comparing a failing single-agent search cycle vs. SearchOS recovery behavior.
Progress tracker timeline visualizing task state across long interaction histories.
Budget vs. output quality chart showing reduced wasted searches and improved completeness.
paper_title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
paper_authors: Yuyao Zhang, Junjie Gao, Zhengxian Wu, Jiaming Fan, Jin Zhang
